objective: For a finitary value law over a finite alphabet Q, with Leibniz's rule (names u and v are one place iff s(ug) = s(vg) for every word g): (T1) the boards are exactly Sch(Stab(s)) for the law's solutions s on the tree; (T2) the strong form S (every board the tree or finite) is false: the horofunction law on Z_3 (a place of value k has exactly one neighbour of value k - 1 and three of value k + 1) allows Sch(<x^3>); (T3, Lemma A) a periodic solution using a branching pattern gives a solution with trivial stabilizer (the tree) and one with an infinite cyclic stabilizer; (T4, Lemma B) if no solution has trivial stabilizer, some isolated solution is invariant under an h != 1 and rigid off h's axis; (T5, the target W) if some board is infinite, the tree is a board; (T6, P) no law makes every board grow quadratically, from W, and unconditionally for the laws T3 covers and for deterministic laws. Or record which fails and why.
title: Boards under Leibniz's rule
